X.from: Gibraltar (Allied HQ). Early frames show civilians leaving. In the last frame, Allied forces arrive from the Atlantic, off the left edge of the map.
X.route: Gibraltar to Casablanca (civilians). Gibraltar to Tangier. Gibraltar to London, Jamaica and Madeira. Allied landings at Casablanca, Oran and Algiers (red arrows from the west), plus aircraft to Oran.
X.where: Gibraltar, at the southern tip of Spain at the Strait, shown with a red dot. It is hard to find in frame 1 because it is small.
X.note: The base map is attractive, with relief shading, a legend and a clear date card. The routes are thin pale lines that disappear against the pale sea. The labels are small for a phone and crowd the route lines. In frame 3 the Jamaica and Madeira labels crowd the date card and the credit line. 'Spain' is labelled twice, on frame 3 and again on frame 2. Frame 4 puts the Gibraltar label on top of the red arrows and the Allied landings box. The camera zoom changes between frames, so the map shifts under the viewer. The Jamaica and Madeira routes run off-screen, so their destinations can't be seen. The legend says 'Britain & Allies' in red, but red appears only in frame 4. The credit line, 'approx. borders c. 1941 — Cliopatria (Seshat)', takes up a lot of space on screen. The civilian evacuation of 1940 and the Allied invasion of 1942 are shown as different kinds of movement but share one frame.

why_split: The 1940 civilian evacuations from Gibraltar and the Nov 1942 Allied landings (Operation Torch) are different stories with different directions of travel, so cramming them into one pan makes the viewer relearn the map.
top_fix: Cut it into two shots: 1940 evacuation, then 1942 landings. Draw routes as thick, high-contrast, animated lines with arrowheads. Zoom in on Gibraltar at the start. Show one label at a time, at larger text size. Keep the red dot pulsing and the date card steady. Drop the credit line to a small footer.
